UNH.rationale: UNH is a dominant healthcare franchise with a strong competitive position, but the fundamental picture is mixed. Q1 2026 showed revenue up 2% YoY to $111.7B and EPS of $6.90 (roughly flat YoY), with the medical care ratio improving to 83.9% from 84.8% — a positive signal on cost management. Operating cash flow was strong at $8.9B (1.4x net income). However, membership declined by 1.1 million, Optum earnings fell 15%, and the company faces ongoing headwinds from Medicare Advantage margin pressure, elevated medical costs, and regulatory/legal risks including a DOJ probe into Optum Rx. The balance sheet is solid (equity $103.9B, debt-to-capital improving to 42.9%), and management is executing on cost discipline, AI investments, and accelerated buybacks ($2B by end of Q2 2026). Valuation is the key tension: the P/E of 26.3x is at the very top of its 365-day range (9.5–26.3), having nearly doubled from ~14x in early April after the Q1 beat and guidance raise. While the forward P/E of ~20x cited by some analysts may look reasonable, the trailing P/E has expanded dramatically, suggesting the market has already priced in much of the recovery narrative. The stock surged 37.7% in the last quarter alone. News sentiment is broadly positive (mean 0.52), and the guidance raise to $18.25+ adjusted EPS is constructive, but the stock's rapid re-rating leaves limited upside at current levels. The near-term catalyst (Q1 beat + guidance raise) has already played out. Net: solid franchise in recovery mode, but valuation has caught up to the improving fundamentals, warranting only a mildly positive score.
